IS* 1927-1980 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
FLAT DRIVING CHAINS 



( First Revision ) 



0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 10 March 1980, after the draft finalized by the 
Spinning Machinery ( Gotton System ) Sectional Committee had been 
approved by the Textile Division Council 

0*2 This standard was first published in 1961 and covered chains of 
36*5 mm pitch for use on slow speed cards. As these cards are not in use 
now, this revision covers the chains suitable for semi-high and high 
production revolving flat cards of various makes. This opportunity has 
also been availed of to cover both riveted chains and chains with deta- 
chable bushes. 

0*3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing 
the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard* 



!♦ SCOPE 

1*1 This standard prescribes requirements for flat driving chains for serni- 
high and high production revolving flat cards. 

2* TYPES 

2*1 The chains shall be either of the following types: 

a) Riveted chain assembly ( see Fig. 1 ), and 

b) Chain assembly with detachable bushes ( see Fig. 2 ) ♦ 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS j 1927* 1980 




Fig* 1 Riveted Flat Driviko Chain 




Fig. 2 Flat Driving Chain with Detachable Bush 



3. MANUFACTURE 



3.1 Material 

rnents; 



The material used shall meet the following require* 



Tensile strength, in case of plates 
Hardness, incase of bushes 



68 kg/mm^ Mitt 
50-60 HRG 



3*2 Freedom from Defects — The chains shall be free from burrs and 
sharp edges. In case of riveted chains, each chain bush shall be riveted 
over at the plain end in such a manner as to allow easy working of the 
chain. The bushes shall be free to rotate in all links. 



18:1927-1980 



4. REQUIREMENTS 

4.X Number of Links — The number of links in the chains shall be 
either 106 or 110 or as agreed between the buyer and the seller, 

4*2 Length of Chain — The length of chain measured under the 
following conditions shall be within +™ mm of the value obtained by 
multiplication of pitch of chain and the number of links; 

The chain shall be placed on a table with one end secured* It 
should be fully extended by attaching a weight of 45 kg at the free 
end over a pulley to take up clearance in the chain link and the 
chain bush* 

4*2.1 When the chains are supplied in pairs, the difference in the 
lengths of the chains in a pair shall not exceed 1*60 mm. 

4*3 Other Dimensions — The chains shall conform to the requirements 
of Table 1 read with Fig. 1 and 2.

4*4 Surface Treatment — The chains shall be galvanized or given a 
suitable treatment for rust prevention. 

5* MARKING 

5*1 Each chain shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or 
trade-mark* 

5*2 Each package of chains shall bear the following information: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark, if any; 

b) Type of chain; 

c) Variety number; and 

d) Number of chains. 

5*2*1 The chains may also be marked with the IS I Certification Mark* 

Not® — The use of the I SI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks } Act and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian 
Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the 
requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and 
quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the pro- 
ducer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence 
for the use of The ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution ,
